description: Measures the FREE-GENERATION regime directly: mask ratios 0.7, 0.95, 0.99, 1.0 x steps {1,8,16,32,64}, both checkpoints (round-4b step_00004000 and the codecpt pre-code baseline), n=256 held-out sequences with bootstrap CIs. WHY: the completed default-grid run (job-bff8b583) found em@32-em@1 POSITIVE at 30/50/70% but -0.0252 at 90%, IDENTICALLY in both checkpoints (-0.0252 vs -0.0252, matching CIs) -- so the high-mask destructiveness is ARCHITECTURAL and predates code training, which retroactively explains why three rounds of corruption-process fixes all returned pass@1 0.0. Free generation is the ~100% mask regime and the grid stopped at 0.9, so the regime that actually matters was never measured; 0.9 -> 1.0 is extrapolation. 0.7 is included as an OVERLAP ANCHOR: it must reproduce the previously measured +0.0097 (4b) / +0.0096 (codecpt), otherwise this run is not comparable and nothing else in it should be believed. NOTE 1.0 is UNCONDITIONAL generation -- no clean context at all -- which is strictly harder than the code task (clean prompt + masked completion), so 0.95/0.99 bracket the real setting better than 1.0 does. READ: if em@1 continues to beat every iterative setting as ratio -> 1.0, a mask-ratio-dependent step schedule (fewer steps, or single-shot, at high mask) is a decode-side fix needing NO retraining, and it is the first Goal-2 intervention with direct measured support. Uses the fixed global document_id labelling plus the post-merge record-count audit (rc=7) that caught the 87.5%-silent-loss bug on its first live run.
